Bug_Title: NP: close() invoked on a value that is always null (NP_CLOSING_NULL)
Bug_Details:
close() is being invoked on a value that is always null. If this statement is executed,
a null pointer exception will occur. But the big risk here you never close
something that should be closed.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by intentionally invoking the close() method on a null Closeable object. This will result in a NullPointerException when the close() method is called.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUnit test case triggers the bug by calling the showBug method of the NullCloseExample class, which attempts to invoke the close() method on a null Closeable object.
